s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disease with skin, joint, and lung involvement
salient_findings: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints (MCPs) and interphalangeal joints (IPs)
Tender ulcerations and skin lesions
Bibasilar rales and interstitial lung disease
Elevated ferritin and lymphocytopenia
Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies
key_facts: 7-month history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, and weight loss
Previous hospitalization for hypoxia
Prior treatment with prednisone
Symmetric joint swelling preventing fist formation
Dorsal MCPs had ulcers, distal fingers were dyspigmented and atrophic
Normal capillaroscopy
Palmar IP creases had ulcerated lichenoid papules
Oxford Scale muscle strength was 5 of 5 throughout
Aldolase: 4.5 U/L (normal)
Creatine kinase: 32 U/L (depressed)
Ferritin: 1543 ng/mL (elevated)
Lymphocytopenia with CD3: 328 μL, CD4: 233 μL, CD8: 85 μL
Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies
Positive immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies (19.5 units)
Negative results for HIV, anti–Scl-70 antibodies, anti–β2-glycoprotein 1 antibodies, lupus anticoagulant, cryoglobulins, anti–Mi-2 antibodies
Normal prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, tissue thromboplastin

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, lymphocytopenia, and multisystem involvement

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Positive immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies and history of hypoxia

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and symptoms of dryness

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and scleroderma features

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multisystem involvement and presence of autoantibodies without a clear diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, and weight loss, along with laboratory findings such as elevated ferritin, lymphocytopenia, and positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus. Additionally, the presence of positive immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies and the patient's history of hypoxia and interstitial lung disease also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has positive immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies, the clinical presentation and other laboratory findings are more consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not primarily suggest Sjögren's Syndrome, which is characterized by exocrine gland inflammation and autoantibodies.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not meet the criteria for Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, which typically involves a combination of features from multiple connective tissue diseases.

rejected.label: Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are more specific and suggestive of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, rather than an undifferentiated connective tissue disease.
